name: PaintClarity
author: paintops

sections.description:
PaintClarity turns your WordPress site into the back office for your painting business. (PaintClarity was formerly known as PaintOps. Same plugin, same team, same data.) Build professional quotes, send them to customers who can view, e-sign, and pay a deposit online, schedule crews on a calendar, track every job from lead to invoice, and, on Pro, see your real profit per job, per crew, and per worker.

It was built by a painter, for painters. The quote builder understands painting scope: interior/exterior components, standard inclusions and exclusions, and the disclaimer language that keeps you out of disputes. Your data lives in your own WordPress database, not locked inside someone else’s SaaS.

Quote to invoice, start to finish

  • Quotes, estimates & bids: a scope-aware builder with reusable inclusions/exclusions, itemized or lump-sum pricing, printable output, and email delivery.
  • A professional customer page: your customer opens a clean, branded page (your logo, your terms & conditions) and accepts by typing their name, an e-signature-grade record with timestamp. They can also decline with a reason, or ask a question, and you’re notified either way.
  • Acceptance converts the quote to a job automatically, whether they paid a deposit online or you shook hands, and a “Mark as Won” button covers the phone call.
  • Invoices: numbered invoices for the balance (full or partial), emailed or shared by link, payable online (Pro + Stripe) or marked paid for check/cash, with the payment logged so balances always agree.
  • Receivables at a glance: unpaid invoices surface on your dashboard with amounts and age.

Running the work

  • Scheduling calendar with crew filtering, worker badges, time-off, and a subscribe link for Google/Apple/Outlook. Add your own recurring holiday labels.
  • Crews: group your painters into named, colored crews; staff a job with one tap and filter the calendar and reports by crew.
  • Job board / pipeline: Quote → Active → Completed, plus a lost-leads drawer with the customer’s decline reason so you can revive the ones worth re-working.
  • A real app for your painters: install-to-home-screen (PWA), a “My Jobs” home, one-tap directions (Google/Apple/Waze), per-job check-in/out that works offline and syncs, photo/receipt/note logging, a “My Hours” view of their own time and pay, and a “Mark Job Complete” button that notifies the office. Workers see only what their permissions allow, never your numbers.
  • Customers: a directory with contact details, lifetime value, job history, and multiple service addresses per customer, built for landlords, realtors, property managers, and GCs whose one account means a dozen properties.
  • Before/After photos with camera alignment overlay and a compare slider.
  • Color Visualizer: load a photo of the house or the room, select the surface, and turn a color wheel until it is the color you are proposing. The wall changes color and keeps its own shading, grain and texture. Select by fill, by matching color, or by dragging a box over a big flat wall. Handles stucco, siding, brick, concrete block and interior drywall, takes the Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore number alongside it, and prints or saves the render for the customer. Runs entirely in your browser: no photo is uploaded anywhere.
  • Trade calculators, paint-color tracking, and resource links.
  • A choice of visual themes (light, dark, industrial, and more) with a modern app-style navigation bar on desktop and phone.

What Pro adds

  • Job financials & profitability: costs, materials, labor hours; gross, expenses, profit, and margin per job; a Profits dashboard with profit-by-classification, profit-per-hour rankings, and profit by crew and by worker (allocated by logged hours).
  • Expenses & receipts against any job, plus business-level and vehicle expense tracking for tax time.
  • Online payments: deposits on quote acceptance and invoice balances through Stripe Checkout, recorded automatically.
  • AI tools (bring your own OpenAI key): estimate dimensions, gallons, and a Description of Work from a photo; scan receipts to auto-fill expenses; get feedback on or a rewrite of your quote wording.

Pro is a paid upgrade handled through Freemius. The free plugin is fully functional on its own; Pro is optional.

Bundled artwork

The four ready-made logos offered under Business > Logo URL (assets/img/logos/) are AI-generated original artwork created for this plugin. They carry no third-party rights and are distributed under the same GPLv2-or-later license as the rest of the plugin. They are optional, off by default, and carry no PaintClarity branding or link.

External services

This plugin can connect to the following third-party services. Some are optional and only run when you enable and configure the corresponding feature.

OpenAI (Pro AI features, optional). When you use an AI feature (Photo Estimate, Receipt Scan, Description-of-Work Feedback or Rewrite), the plugin sends the relevant input, the photo you choose to upload and/or the quote text you are working on, to the OpenAI API using your own OpenAI API key, and receives the generated result. No data is sent unless you click one of these buttons. PaintClarity does not store the photo. Requests go to https://api.openai.com. See OpenAI’s Terms (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use) and Privacy Policy (https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy).

Stripe (Pro online payments, optional). If you enable card payments and a customer pays online, the plugin creates a Stripe Checkout session and verifies Stripe’s webhook using your own Stripe keys. Order/amount details are exchanged with Stripe to process the payment. Requests go to https://api.stripe.com. See Stripe’s Services Agreement (https://stripe.com/legal/ssa) and Privacy Policy (https://stripe.com/privacy).

Google Maps Platform (optional). If you add a Google Maps API key, address fields use Google Places/Geocoding for autocomplete and validation, and job locations may be shown on an embedded map. The address text you type is sent to Google to return suggestions. Requests go to https://maps.googleapis.com and related Google Maps endpoints. See Google’s Terms (https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy). (One-tap turn-by-turn Directions for your crew use keyless map links and need no API key.)

YouTube and Vimeo (Resources page video embeds, optional). The Resources page (staff-facing, inside your admin area) lets you save links to training videos, and seeds a starter list of publicly available painting tutorials on YouTube. When a staff member clicks a saved YouTube or Vimeo link’s play button, the video is embedded on the page via the provider’s standard embed player (www.youtube.com / player.vimeo.com), which loads content from that provider and is subject to its terms; no data is sent until the play button is clicked, and you can delete any or all saved links. See YouTube’s Terms (https://www.youtube.com/t/terms) and Google’s Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy), and Vimeo’s Terms (https://vimeo.com/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://vimeo.com/privacy).

Freemius (licensing & updates). PaintClarity uses the Freemius SDK to manage Pro licenses, deliver Pro updates, and (optionally) collect anonymous usage diagnostics you can opt out of. Site and license information is exchanged with Freemius. See Freemius’s Terms (https://freemius.com/terms/) and Privacy Policy (https://freemius.com/privacy/).

You control every one of these by whether you enter the corresponding API key and enable the feature. With no keys entered, PaintClarity runs entirely on your own site.
sections.installation:
1. Install PaintClarity from the Plugins screen (Plugins → Add New → search “PaintClarity”), or upload the plugin ZIP under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin. Activate it.
  2. Create a WordPress Page and add the shortcode [paintops_app]. This one page is your whole PaintClarity app; it routes internally.
  3. Go to PaintClarity → Settings and set your Company Profile (business name, logo, country, currency), and review the Setup Health panel.
  4. (Optional) Add team members under PaintClarity → Painters/Helpers, set their permissions, and group them into Crews.
  5. (Optional) Add your Quote Terms & Conditions under Business Settings so customers see and sign against them.
  6. (Optional, Pro) Under Settings → AI Settings connect OpenAI, under Stripe Payments add your Stripe secret key AND webhook signing secret (both are required before online payment buttons appear), and add a Google Maps API key for address autocomplete.
sections.faq:
Do I need a paid account to use it?

No. The free plugin runs entirely on your own WordPress site and lets you quote, schedule, and manage unlimited jobs. Pro is an optional upgrade.

What happens to my data if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Nothing is deleted. Your jobs, quotes, customers, payments, hours, and photos stay in your WordPress database, so nothing is lost if you deactivate temporarily or reinstall later. If you truly want the data gone, delete the plugin’s tables and its uploads from your database and media library.

Does it work without OpenAI, Stripe, or Google Maps?

Yes. Those are optional integrations. If you don’t enter their keys, the related features simply stay off and everything else works, including keyless turn-by-turn directions for your crew.

Can my customers really sign a quote online?

They accept by typing their full name, which is stored with a timestamp and IP address alongside your Terms & Conditions, a solid acceptance record. They can also decline with a reason, and change their minds later.

Who pays for the AI usage?

You do, through your own OpenAI account and key, typically a fraction of a cent to a few cents per action. PaintClarity adds per-month usage caps you control so costs stay predictable.

Can my painters log in without seeing my numbers?

Yes. Painters/Helpers get a dedicated role with opt-in permissions and their own app view: My Jobs, My Hours (their own time and pay only), directions, check-in/out, photos and receipts. Financial figures are owner-level and hidden from workers unless you explicitly grant access.

Does it work in the field with bad reception?

The app installs to a phone’s home screen, and Time Clock check-in/out keeps working offline and syncs when a connection returns.

Where is my data stored?

In your own WordPress database. PaintClarity doesn’t host your business data on an external server.
sections.changelog:
1.2.038

  • The New Job button on the Jobs page is aligned properly on a laptop and on a phone. The title now sits on its own line with one rule under it, and the button and the View All / Board links sit in a clean row beneath, the same shape as the Expenses page.

1.2.037

  • The Profits page reads properly on a phone. The year cards used to hold the stats beside the big Profit figure no matter how narrow the screen got, which squeezed them to nothing: every label was cut to two letters (“SALES TA…”) and the dollar figures ran into each other. On a phone the card now stacks, Profit first, with the stats under it in as many columns as actually fit.
  • Same fix on a small laptop window. At 1024px the stat strip was holding five columns in the space for three and clipping the same way.
  • The Top and Bottom jobs ranking no longer pushes the whole app sideways on a very narrow phone.

1.2.036

  • One load control in the Visualizer, not two. While the photo area is empty it is the button; once a photo is in, the toolbar button comes back as “Change photo”, which is what it does at that point.
  • New Job at the top of the Jobs page.
  • File a Receipt at the top of the Expenses page.

1.2.035

  • The empty photo area in the Visualizer is now the button. Tap or click anywhere in it to load a photo, instead of reaching back up to the toolbar. On a desktop you can also drop a file straight onto it.
  • Take a photo with the camera. On a phone the empty area offers “Take a Photo” alongside “Choose a Photo”, so you can shoot the wall you are standing in front of rather than hunting for it in your library.
  • Selection tolerance moved up again, to directly under the file name. The hint you read once should not sit above the slider you drag all day.

1.2.034

  • All three receipt forms now open the same way. Business Related asks “Scan Receipt with AI” or “Manually Enter” first, the way the vehicle and job forms already did, instead of dropping a full form on you with the scan button buried inside it.
  • Removed the “File a Vehicle Receipt” button from the Vehicle Log. It sat directly above the form it linked to.

1.2.033

  • One menu on a phone. The hamburger beside the search box is gone; the bottom bar and its More sheet are the menu. Everything the hamburger reached is in the sheet, including Checkup, which it was missing, plus your version, who you are signed in as, and the WP Admin link for administrators. Tablets keep the hamburger, because they have no bottom bar.
  • Renamed “Completed & all jobs” to “View All Jobs”.

1.2.032

  • Deleting a job now clears everything it owns. Quote add-ons were being left behind entirely, and so were logged messages. Photos, notes, receipts and their images, the time clock, financials, payments, paint colors, invoices, follow-up visits and quotes all go, verified table by table against a test job built with one of everything.
  • An overhead expense or a vehicle trip that was tagged to a deleted job keeps the record and loses the tag. Neither is the job’s money, so neither is removed.
  • Every delete in the app is now a button rather than a link: business notes, vehicle log entries, automatic vehicle costs, and the permanent job delete. A link that deletes can be fetched twice, which is what was swallowing the confirmations, and could be fired by anything that follows a URL.
  • New vendor names now match what is already on your books. Type a name that differs only in capitalization or spacing and it saves under the spelling you already use. Type something close, like sherwin-williams when Sherwin-Williams is on file, and the form offers it before you save. Your choice either way, and once you take it the next receipt matches on its own.
  • The Expenses page sections fold, one open at a time: Where it went, Month by month, Who you paid.
  • The duplicate receipt finder moved from Business to Expenses, next to the spending it asks about.
  • Taxes & Filing reads shorter. The explanation of what goes in each tax bucket is still there, folded into About this data.
  • Removed two database queries that ran on every visit to the Business page and fed nothing.

1.2.031

  • Business overhead is back on the Business page. The list of logged overhead, with its edit and delete, now lives inside the Business Expenses & Overhead section where it used to be, instead of on a page of its own. Filing a receipt is still File a Receipt’s job.
  • The Expenses page is now a summary of the year. Job materials, vehicle and overhead side by side with what each one did against last year, every category ranked largest first, who you paid ranked by size, and a month by month list you can open and check against a card statement.
  • Fixed: deleting an overhead expense never showed its confirmation. The app’s offline worker was fetching the delete link a second time, and the second fetch, finding the row already gone, drew the page with nothing to say. Deleting is now a button rather than a link and confirms properly.
  • Fixed: opening a section on the Business page. Two sections claimed to open by default and three more worked out which should open only after they had already been drawn, so the section you got was whichever came first in the file. The page now decides once, before anything is drawn.

1.2.030

  • File a Receipt is now the one place every receipt starts. Vehicle, Business Related and Job Cost each have their own form on that page, folded into three cards with one open at a time. Landing there opens none of them, because the question the page asks is which kind of receipt this is.
  • Links can still go straight to the right form. A job’s Add Expense page is unchanged, and the Vehicle page has a new File a Vehicle Receipt button that lands on the vehicle form with it already open.
  • Fixed: on the Business Related form, picking “+ New vendor” did not open the box to type the name in, and the Scan with AI button did nothing. Both had been broken since the form moved to this page in 1.2.027.

1.2.029

  • The Board and Row view switch now agrees with itself. The link text was being drawn before the click was processed, so it showed the view you had just left. The view itself was always right; only the label was a click behind.
  • Moving a card on the Job Board now says so. Mark as Job, Mark as Not Won, Mark Completed and Back to Request all rewrote the record and then the card simply vanished from its column, which looks the same as a click that did nothing. Each one now names the record and what it became.
  • The folded sections on the Jobs page have a light outline, so a closed section reads as a card that is shut rather than a line of text floating on the page.

1.2.028

  • The Business page is a stack of accordions again, one open at a time. Taxes & Filing is first and opens by default, because it is what you came for; the roster and the vehicle list are reference and stay folded until you want them.
  • The Vendors & 1099 table finally works on a phone. Each vendor is a card with its own labels instead of a seven-column table dragged sideways, so the two decisions you are there to make are a tap each.
  • “Do not track” is now “1099 not needed”. The decision you are recording is about the form, not about the vendor.
  • The 1099 threshold moved to PaintClarity > Business > 1099 Reporting. It is a setting, not something you do while reading a vendor list, and it had been sitting inside that list’s Save button making it look like the button only saved the number beside it. The Business page now shows one line saying which figure is in force and why.
  • The rest of that block is regrouped: saving says what it saves, the bulk action is named in plain words and asks before it writes, and the two accountant exports sit apart under their own label.
  • Two lines of page furniture removed: the paragraph describing the Business page to someone already on it, and the sentence explaining the year switch sitting directly below the year switch.

1.2.027

  • File a Receipt is now genuinely the one front door for every receipt. The overhead form used to live on the Expenses page and had to be summoned with a second parameter, so the one-front-door page had one door that opened onto a different building. The form is on File a Receipt itself now, at one route with one parameter.
  • The Expenses page is the ledger and nothing else: what has been logged this tax year, and editing or deleting a row in it. Its File a Receipt button goes straight to the overhead form.
  • If overhead is the only place you can file a receipt, File a Receipt takes you straight to the form instead of asking a question with one answer, the same way it already did for a lone job or the vehicle log.

1.2.026

  • Quotes Out and Needs Your Attention now stay folded until you open them. They were set to open themselves whenever something was in them, which on a working business is every day, so neither was ever actually seen folded. The counts in each heading are what tell you whether to look.
  • Receipt search moved from the Business page to File a Receipt. Checking whether a stack of paper receipts is already filed is a filing job, so it now sits on the filing page, right above the chooser you use when the answer is no. The duplicate finder stays on Business, where the year picker it uses lives.
  • The Expenses page is a ledger again. The add form sits behind a File a Receipt button, which is the one front door for a job receipt, a vehicle receipt or an overhead receipt.
  • The Scan Receipt with AI and Manually Enter buttons above that form are gone. The form has its own Scan with AI button on the receipt photo field, so those two asked a question about a choice the form already offered. Picking a photo still starts a scan on its own.

1.2.025

  • Message History can now start the next contact, not just write down the last one. Call, Text and Email open your own phone or mail app and log themselves into the history below; Email Quote, Send Follow-Up Email and Text Follow-Up are the same composed sends the quote screen and the alerts card already offer, shown only when they actually apply to the record.
  • Record a contact folds away on that page. It was six fields sitting above the history, so reading what had already happened started with a scroll past a form nobody had asked for. It reopens by itself if an entry fails to save.
  • The Communication section on Jobs folds away too, alongside Quotes Out and Needs Your Attention.
  • Mark quote declined now appears only when there is something to decline: a request with a quote on it the customer has not accepted. A request nobody has priced and an already accepted quote no longer offer the button, and the same test is enforced when the form is submitted, not just when it is drawn.
  • The Communication section’s replies say whether they worked. Four of its five messages are refusals and every one of them was being drawn in the green success box.
  • Today’s Crew is gone from the Jobs page. It listed the jobs scheduled for today, all of which were already in Active Jobs at the top of the same page with more detail; on the commonest day it was a card that existed to say nothing was scheduled.

1.2.024

  • The Jobs page is now organized by what you can do about it. Active Jobs and Upcoming come first and are always open; Quotes Out and Needs Your Attention fold away underneath, opening on their own when there is something in them worth looking at.
  • Every job list has column headers now, so the date, the crew and the value are labeled instead of guessed at. On a phone, where the rows stack, each value keeps its own small label.
  • Wrapping Up is gone. Every row it drew was already in Needs Your Attention one heading higher, and it was drawing them from the same two scans, doubling the work the page did on every load. Its Collect link and its Actions menu moved up into Needs Your Attention, so nothing you could reach from it is lost.
  • Two bugs went with it. Staff who are not allowed to see money were reading balances in Wrapping Up that were hidden from them in the card above. And a completed job that already had an unpaid invoice was counted twice, once as a job and once as an invoice, which is the double-counted total the September 16 fix corrected in one place and not the other.
  • New Communication section at the foot of Jobs: the last contact logged against each open job and quote, and a picker to start the next one. Pending quotes are in the picker too.
  • From that same picker you can mark a quote declined. It moves out of Quotes Out and into Not Won, where Board view’s Back to Request brings it back if the customer changes their mind.
  • Request Performance moved to a page of its own, reached from the acceptance rate shown on the New Quote screen, where the number is worth a glance before you price something. It charts the rate by year and keeps the year by year figures in a show and hide underneath.
  • Completed & all jobs and the Board and Row switch moved up beside the Jobs heading on a wide screen, instead of sitting at the bottom under three lists of rows.

1.2.023

  • The 1099 threshold now follows the year you are reporting on. The IRS figure was $600 for payments made through 2025 and is $2,000 from 2026, so those two years are no longer judged against the same number. If your site still had the old $600 sitting in it only because that used to be the shipped default, it is cleared for you. Type your own figure any time to override it.
  • The Upgrade to Pro button turned purple once you had clicked it. It was falling through to the browser’s default link colors.
  • Color Visualizer: selection tolerance moved out of the right rail to sit directly under the photo, where you can see what it is doing while you drag it. This matters most on a phone, where the rail sits below the photo entirely. Its minimum is now 1 instead of 4, for finer cuts.
  • Color Visualizer: the color card moved above the surface card. Colors get changed over and over while trying options in front of a customer; the surface is set once.
  • The AI Job Photo Estimator moved above the Description of Work instead of sitting in a drawer below it. It writes that field, so it now comes before it.
  • The estimator has its own box to say what is being painted, with guidance. It used to quietly send whatever was in the Description of Work, which on a new quote was nothing at all.
  • The estimator’s result is more compact. Paint and supplies sit side by side, and the write-up with its Insert buttons sits directly under the figures instead of a screen below them.

1.2.022

  • Housekeeping, no change you can see. The three big settings screens, Business, Painters/Helpers and Settings, moved out of the main plugin file into their own file. They work exactly as before. This keeps the main file small enough for our build system to package correctly.

1.2.020

  • Housekeeping. The plugin now states where its own updates come from, so a Pro install is never offered the free version by mistake. Nothing you can see has changed.

1.2.019

  • New: Message History on every job, in the job menu directly above Call Customer and Text Customer. Every way you talked to this customer about this job, in one list, newest first. Reading the history and making contact are the same errand, so they sit together as one group.
  • Record what happened outside the app: a call from your own phone, a text thread, an email you pasted into your mail app, a conversation on site. Mark whether you contacted them or they contacted you, set the date it actually happened rather than today, and write down what was agreed.
  • Every entry says how much it is worth. “Sent by PaintClarity” means the app composed it and handed it to your mail server. “Link opened” means somebody tapped a call or text link and what happened next is anyone’s guess. “Recorded by hand” means a person says it happened. Those first two used to look identical, which quietly overstated the second.
  • Your crew can record a contact on a job they are on, which is often the only way a driveway conversation ever gets written down. They do not see the history back; customer contact history stays in the office.
  • Anything PaintClarity sent itself can never be edited or deleted, by anyone. A record you can rewrite is not a record. Entries written by hand can be corrected, and a corrected entry says it was edited, when, and by whom.
  • Quotes, invoices, payment reminders, follow-ups and review requests have been logging themselves since July. That history was only ever visible in a collapsed drawer at the bottom of the job page that showed nothing when empty, so most people never found it. It has a real page now.
  • The panel on the job page shows even when a job has nothing logged, and says so, rather than disappearing. It carries the same marks the full page does, so you can tell at a glance whether a line was sent by PaintClarity or is somebody’s account of a call.
  • The record-a-contact form is properly laid out. Fields line up on one baseline, labels read as labels, and the date and notes boxes match every other field in the app instead of being whatever the browser drew.
  • Two field types, date-and-time and multi-line notes, were missing from the app’s form styling everywhere, not just here. They now match the rest, including the larger touch targets phones need.

1.2.016

  • The review request now delivers the customer their paint colors. Color, product, sheen and where each one went, in the same email that asks for the review. Give and get at the same time.
  • Colors have only ever been recorded for your crew. Sending them turns a pure request into something the customer actually wants to receive, and it answers in advance the call every painter gets two years later asking what was on the hallway wall. That email then sits in their inbox with your name on it and the exact product, which is where they look when they want the trim done.
  • How many gallons is deliberately left out. That is a purchasing note, it reads like a line on a bill to a homeowner, and it is no use to them when they want to match a color later.
  • A job with no colors logged sends exactly the email it sends today, with no empty heading and no gap. Rows with nothing but a location are skipped.
  • Place the list yourself with {paint_colors}, or leave your message as it is: one written before this existed does not need editing, the colors go in just after your review link. There is a switch under Settings > Google Reviews to turn the whole thing off.
  • The preview on the send screen is the email. What you read there is what goes out, colors included.

1.2.015

  • New: Vendors and 1099, under Business. Everyone the business paid in a year, added up from job receipts, business overhead, and the hours of anyone you have marked as paid on a subcontractor basis, ranked biggest first.
  • Subcontractor hours count. For most painting shops the real 1099 money is the person paid by the hour who is not on payroll, and those dollars live in the time log rather than in the receipts. Tick “Paid as sub” next to someone on Painters/Helpers and their hours roll up like any other vendor, at the rate stamped when the hours were logged, so a raise in March cannot restate January.
  • Record a decision per vendor once and it sticks: Track for 1099, 1099 not needed, or Undecided. Vendors over the threshold that nobody has ruled on are pulled to the top and highlighted, so a paint store you will never 1099 stops competing for attention with the drywall sub you will.
  • Different capitalization and spacing fold together on their own, so “Sherwin Williams” and “sherwin williams” are one line. For the ones that cannot fold automatically, “Same as” folds two rows into one for good.
  • A printable sheet to hand your accountant, and a CSV to send them.
  • It says plainly what it cannot do: whether a payment is reportable depends on the vendor’s business type, whether you bought services or goods, and whether it went out on a card, none of which the app can know. It totals the year accurately and holds your decisions. It does not fill in a form.
  • Spend on jobs marked “exclude from reports” stays out of the totals, as it does in every accountant-facing report here, but the amount is named on the page instead of disappearing quietly.
  • Fixed: on PHP 8.4 the Export Data download wrote PHP deprecation warnings into the .csv file itself, so the export opened with warning text mixed into the rows.

1.2.014

  • New: the job form now checks your crew before you save. Tick a worker who has approved time off during the job and the box will not stay ticked, with the days named. Tick someone already booked on another job in that window and you get a warning naming the job and the dates, and you decide: a supervisor covering three jobs on one schedule, or two callbacks in a day, is normal work and is not blocked.
  • Time off and overlapping jobs are both checked live, as you change the dates, the length, or who is on the job, on a new job and on one you are editing.
  • The check reads the whole job, not just its first day. A three-day job that runs over someone’s Thursday off is caught now; the old check only looked at the start date, only ran on jobs already saved, and never looked at time off at all.
  • Repeating time off is respected across years, so a standing day off still blocks a booking on next year’s calendar.
  • The old note on the job form saying conflicts were not checked until the job was saved is gone, because it is no longer true.

1.2.013

  • New: optional add-ons on a quote. Quote the work the customer has decided on, then offer the rest as tick boxes they check when they sign. The homeowner who wants the living room and kitchen now, and is undecided about the bedrooms, gets one quote instead of two. Add them under “Optional add-ons” on the quote form with a title, description, price and your cost.
  • On the customer’s quote page the add-ons appear as tappable cards. Ticking one updates the total and the deposit on the spot, and whatever is ticked when they type their name is what they have agreed to and what the quote total becomes.
  • Accepted add-ons are itemized on the quote document, so the signed paperwork says what was bought and not just a larger number, and the amount printed is the amount charged at the time, even if your tax rate changes later.
  • Your cost for each add-on feeds the job’s expected profit, so selling one raises revenue and costs together. An add-on priced with no cost is caught: Job Pulse leaves expected profit off rather than reporting it too high by the whole add-on, and tells you which one to fix.
  • The quote view shows what was accepted and what was passed on, so the office knows what the crew is walking into.
  • An accepted add-on is locked on the quote form: editing the quote afterwards cannot reprice or delete something the customer has already signed for.

1.2.012

  • The app now says which build you are on: “PaintClarity Free” or “PaintClarity Pro”, in the sidebar, the sidebar footer, and the version lines in Business Settings. A Pro copy with no active license reads Free, because that is what it can actually do.
  • Fixed: clicking the Complete / Not Complete pill on a job worked, but left you on a broken half-loaded page with no confirmation. The job flipped and the date was recorded correctly; it was the page afterward that failed. It now lands cleanly on the job with “Marked complete.” (or “Marked as not complete.”), and a refresh can no longer flip the job a second time.

1.2.011

  • Job Pulse is honest now when nobody is logging hours. Plenty of shops do not run a clock, and the page used to answer anyway: a job with nothing on the clock showed a pace, a projection built from zero, and a per-hour figure in the hundreds of thousands. Pace, per-hour and the projection are left out when there are no real hours, and the page says so and says what still holds (revenue, costs, profit and what is owed never depended on hours).
  • Fixed: being far behind the schedule’s hours was marked green. Running over is a warning, running level is good, and running well under is now neither, because it can mean an efficient crew or it can mean hours are not being logged and the page cannot tell which.
  • Fixed: a job could report that “every hour was logged by someone with no hourly rate on file” when no hours had been logged at all.
  • The “What this job is telling you” lines now carry a mark and a verdict: Went well, Worth watching, Needs attention, or Worth knowing for the lines that are a statement rather than a pass or a fail. The colored edge alone asked you to already know what green and red meant.
  • The AI’s “Next time” advice has to be an instruction you can act on, naming what to change on the next quote, instead of repeating this job’s hours and days back as though that were the advice.

1.2.010

  • Sales tax, VAT, gross receipts tax: whatever it is called where you work, it is now tagged per JOB rather than applied to everything. Painting is not taxed in Florida, is taxed in California and South Dakota, is hit with gross receipts tax in New Mexico, and carries VAT in Germany, and a shop near a line works both sides of one. Set your rate (and what to call it) under Business Settings > Pricing Rules, then tick “Has 6.5% tax” on the jobs it applies to. Add more rates if you work more than one jurisdiction and the job form offers a picker instead.
  • Tax you collect is no longer counted as money you earned. Profit, margin, profit per hour, the Profits page, crew and classification reports, job rankings, customer lifetime value, Job Pulse and the job coversheet all read the job net of tax now, and the Business Financial Report shows what you collected, the tax inside it, and your actual income as three separate lines for your accountant. What the customer owes is unchanged: the quote, deposit, invoice and balance due all still include the tax, because they still owe it.
  • A job keeps the rate and the name it was tagged with. Changing or retiring a rate later never restates a year you have already filed.
  • Nothing changes at all if you do not charge tax. Leave the rate at 0 and no tax option appears anywhere.
  • Fixed: the credit card fee was written on every quote and never actually charged. There is now a switch for it. Off (the default) means no fee is added and the quote stops mentioning one. On means the fee shows as its own line on the payment page, and the quote, the deposit page and the pay button all say what it is before your customer commits. The fee is not counted as income on the job, the same as your processor’s cut is …

short_description: Run your painting business from WordPress: quotes to invoices, crews, scheduling, customers, photos, profit reports, optional AI and card payments.
description:
PaintClarity turns your WordPress site into the back office for your painting business. (PaintClarity was formerly known as PaintOps. Same plugin, same team, same data.) Build professional quotes, send them to customers who can view, e-sign, and pay a deposit online, schedule crews on a calendar, track every job from lead to invoice, and, on Pro, see your real profit per job, per crew, and per worker.

It was built by a painter, for painters. The quote builder understands painting scope: interior/exterior components, standard inclusions and exclusions, and the disclaimer language that keeps you out of disputes. Your data lives in your own WordPress database, not locked inside someone else’s SaaS.

Quote to invoice, start to finish

  • Quotes, estimates & bids: a scope-aware builder with reusable inclusions/exclusions, itemized or lump-sum pricing, printable output, and email delivery.
  • A professional customer page: your customer opens a clean, branded page (your logo, your terms & conditions) and accepts by typing their name, an e-signature-grade record with timestamp. They can also decline with a reason, or ask a question, and you’re notified either way.
  • Acceptance converts the quote to a job automatically, whether they paid a deposit online or you shook hands, and a “Mark as Won” button covers the phone call.
  • Invoices: numbered invoices for the balance (full or partial), emailed or shared by link, payable online (Pro + Stripe) or marked paid for check/cash, with the payment logged so balances always agree.
  • Receivables at a glance: unpaid invoices surface on your dashboard with amounts and age.

Running the work

  • Scheduling calendar with crew filtering, worker badges, time-off, and a subscribe link for Google/Apple/Outlook. Add your own recurring holiday labels.
  • Crews: group your painters into named, colored crews; staff a job with one tap and filter the calendar and reports by crew.
  • Job board / pipeline: Quote → Active → Completed, plus a lost-leads drawer with the customer’s decline reason so you can revive the ones worth re-working.
  • A real app for your painters: install-to-home-screen (PWA), a “My Jobs” home, one-tap directions (Google/Apple/Waze), per-job check-in/out that works offline and syncs, photo/receipt/note logging, a “My Hours” view of their own time and pay, and a “Mark Job Complete” button that notifies the office. Workers see only what their permissions allow, never your numbers.
  • Customers: a directory with contact details, lifetime value, job history, and multiple service addresses per customer, built for landlords, realtors, property managers, and GCs whose one account means a dozen properties.
  • Before/After photos with camera alignment overlay and a compare slider.
  • Color Visualizer: load a photo of the house or the room, select the surface, and turn a color wheel until it is the color you are proposing. The wall changes color and keeps its own shading, grain and texture. Select by fill, by matching color, or by dragging a box over a big flat wall. Handles stucco, siding, brick, concrete block and interior drywall, takes the Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore number alongside it, and prints or saves the render for the customer. Runs entirely in your browser: no photo is uploaded anywhere.
  • Trade calculators, paint-color tracking, and resource links.
  • A choice of visual themes (light, dark, industrial, and more) with a modern app-style navigation bar on desktop and phone.

What Pro adds

  • Job financials & profitability: costs, materials, labor hours; gross, expenses, profit, and margin per job; a Profits dashboard with profit-by-classification, profit-per-hour rankings, and profit by crew and by worker (allocated by logged hours).
  • Expenses & receipts against any job, plus business-level and vehicle expense tracking for tax time.
  • Online payments: deposits on quote acceptance and invoice balances through Stripe Checkout, recorded automatically.
  • AI tools (bring your own OpenAI key): estimate dimensions, gallons, and a Description of Work from a photo; scan receipts to auto-fill expenses; get feedback on or a rewrite of your quote wording.

Pro is a paid upgrade handled through Freemius. The free plugin is fully functional on its own; Pro is optional.

Bundled artwork

The four ready-made logos offered under Business > Logo URL (assets/img/logos/) are AI-generated original artwork created for this plugin. They carry no third-party rights and are distributed under the same GPLv2-or-later license as the rest of the plugin. They are optional, off by default, and carry no PaintClarity branding or link.

External services

This plugin can connect to the following third-party services. Some are optional and only run when you enable and configure the corresponding feature.

OpenAI (Pro AI features, optional). When you use an AI feature (Photo Estimate, Receipt Scan, Description-of-Work Feedback or Rewrite), the plugin sends the relevant input, the photo you choose to upload and/or the quote text you are working on, to the OpenAI API using your own OpenAI API key, and receives the generated result. No data is sent unless you click one of these buttons. PaintClarity does not store the photo. Requests go to https://api.openai.com. See OpenAI’s Terms (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use) and Privacy Policy (https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy).

Stripe (Pro online payments, optional). If you enable card payments and a customer pays online, the plugin creates a Stripe Checkout session and verifies Stripe’s webhook using your own Stripe keys. Order/amount details are exchanged with Stripe to process the payment. Requests go to https://api.stripe.com. See Stripe’s Services Agreement (https://stripe.com/legal/ssa) and Privacy Policy (https://stripe.com/privacy).

Google Maps Platform (optional). If you add a Google Maps API key, address fields use Google Places/Geocoding for autocomplete and validation, and job locations may be shown on an embedded map. The address text you type is sent to Google to return suggestions. Requests go to https://maps.googleapis.com and related Google Maps endpoints. See Google’s Terms (https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy). (One-tap turn-by-turn Directions for your crew use keyless map links and need no API key.)

YouTube and Vimeo (Resources page video embeds, optional). The Resources page (staff-facing, inside your admin area) lets you save links to training videos, and seeds a starter list of publicly available painting tutorials on YouTube. When a staff member clicks a saved YouTube or Vimeo link’s play button, the video is embedded on the page via the provider’s standard embed player (www.youtube.com / player.vimeo.com), which loads content from that provider and is subject to its terms; no data is sent until the play button is clicked, and you can delete any or all saved links. See YouTube’s Terms (https://www.youtube.com/t/terms) and Google’s Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy), and Vimeo’s Terms (https://vimeo.com/terms) and Privacy Policy (https://vimeo.com/privacy).

Freemius (licensing & updates). PaintClarity uses the Freemius SDK to manage Pro licenses, deliver Pro updates, and (optionally) collect anonymous usage diagnostics you can opt out of. Site and license information is exchanged with Freemius. See Freemius’s Terms (https://freemius.com/terms/) and Privacy Policy (https://freemius.com/privacy/).

You control every one of these by whether you enter the corresponding API key and enable the feature. With no keys entered, PaintClarity runs entirely on your own site.
